comparch.technical-specification: Redirector is a single lookup path over an ETS-cached, Postgres-backed link table, split into a foundation lookup engine and a cache layer in front of it.
comparch.private-surface: Internal cache invalidation on link creation/retirement; nothing else calls into it directly.
comparch.failure-surface: A cache miss falls through to Postgres; a target being unreachable never fails the redirect itself, only the caller's own follow-through.

permission.name: read_links
permission.description: Read link rows to resolve a short code.

policy.name: No blocking calls in the redirect path
policy.trigger: Any change to the resolve/1 call path.
policy.rationale: Redirect is the hot path every other tool depends on; a blocking call here becomes everyone else's latency.

subcomponent.name: LookupEngine
subcomponent.purpose: The authoritative short-code-to-target lookup over Postgres.

owned-invariants.invariant: A lookup for an unknown code returns :not_found, never an error.
A lookup never blocks on a click-count write.

primary-operations.operation: Look up a short code's target.
Record a click against a short code.
Report a code as retired once its link is gone.

subcomponent.responsibilities: Owns the redirect resolution responsibility end to end.

subcomponent.name: CacheLayer
subcomponent.purpose: An in-memory front for lookup_engine's hot codes.

owned-invariants.invariant: A cache entry is never served past its link's own retirement.
A cache miss always falls through, never returns :not_found on its own word.

primary-operations.operation: Fall through to lookup_engine on a miss.

subcomponent.responsibilities: Speeds up lookup_engine's own responsibility; owns none of its own.

implementation.exit-plan: Remove the cache layer entirely; lookup_engine alone still satisfies every invariant, just slower.
